title: Differentiating between Wealth Held by Households in Public Versus in Private Housing, and Measures to Sustain or Improve Upward Mobility Rates
what_it_is: Differentiating between Wealth Held by Households in Public Versus in Private Housing, and Measures to Sustain or Improve Upward Mobility Rates

sections.label: Housing wealth inequality and mobility questions
sections.summary: Questions ask whether owner-occupied and private housing wealth are differentiated in inequality measurement and what sustains upward mobility rates.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh
sentences.text: asked the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (a) whether the Ministry differentiates between wealth held in owner-occupied public housing and privately-owned housing in measuring household wealth inequality, given the differences in liquidity and ease of deployment arising from resale conditions and use-of-proceeds rules; and (b) if so, how this is taken into account in assessing households' economic resilience and in the computation of wealth Gini coefficient.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: asked the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance in respect of the Ministry's Occasional Paper on income growth, inequality and social mobility trends which indicated that three in four children born into the bottom 20 percent of households in the late 1970s and 1980s moved to higher income tiers as adults, what measures are in place to sustain or improve these upward mobility rates for today's and future cohorts.

sections.label: No new asset disclosure powers
sections.summary: There are no plans to seek powers for more granular asset disclosures, this is the first wealth Gini compilation, and the next survey is in 2028.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: We have no plans at this point to seek additional legislative or administrative powers to require more granular asset disclosures solely for inequality measurement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: This is our first compilation of the wealth Gini coefficient and we do not have a historical series.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: The next cycle of the Household Expenditure Survey is planned for 2028.

sections.label: Top wealth shares
sections.summary: The top 1% hold about 14% of total household wealth and the top 5% about 33%, comparable to similar advanced economies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: The top 1% hold about 14% of total household wealth, while the top 5% holds about 33%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: These levels are broadly comparable to advanced economies with similar wealth Gini coefficients.

sections.label: Commitment on inequality and mobility
sections.summary: Tackling inequality and improving mobility requires sustained investment across generations, with fiscal measures reviewed and updated to remain effective and sustainable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: Tackling inequality and improving mobility requires sustained investment across generations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: We will continue to review and update our fiscal measures to ensure they remain effective and sustainable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: We remain committed to ensuring every Singaporeans can start well, progress in life and share in our nation's success.

sections.label: First wealth Gini measurement
sections.summary: The wealth Gini was measured using survey and administrative data for the first time, and wealth data depends on the five-yearly household expenditure survey.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: We have done so to our best effort, combining both survey data with administrative data, as I have explained in my speech.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: This is the first time we are measuring the wealth Gini coefficient and we are open to improving it over time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: In terms of household income trends, we already publish that data regularly, annually, in the Key Household Income Trends Report.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: But for the wealth Gini coefficient and wealth data, it is dependent on the main source, which is the household expenditure survey, which we do every five years.

sections.label: Looking at data trends
sections.summary: The important part of using this data is to look at the trending.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: In terms of what we would do with this data, I think the important part is to look at the trending.

sections.label: Support for lower-income families
sections.summary: Families, especially in the bottom quintile, have multiple needs and require multiple support, so a package of measures including enhanced ComLink+ is being worked on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: The families, in particular in the bottom quintile, have multiple needs and need multiple support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: And that is why we have been working on a package of various measures, including the enhancement of ComLink+ which the Prime Minister spoke about in his Budget Speech.

sections.label: Property tax and payment deferral
sections.summary: Investment and higher-value properties are taxed higher, single-property homeowners lower with rebates, and asset-rich income-poor seniors can defer property tax via interest-free instalments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: Investment properties and higher-value properties are taxed higher and homeowners with only one property are taxed lower and they receive property tax rebates when necessary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: But we nevertheless understand the concerns that individual property owners may face different financial circumstances, particularly on cash flow.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: So, for asset rich but income poor seniors, we have deferral mechanisms for property tax payments to ease their cash flow pressures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: For instance, eligible seniors and retirees can apply to pay via extended interest-free instalments.

sections.label: No simulation on separating property investment
sections.summary: No simulations have been done on separating investment of property from owner-occupied property.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: On whether or not we have done simulations on separating investment of property from owner-occupied property, we have not done so.
